brief: C interface to Zymkey Application Utilities Library.
intro:
This file contains the C API to the the Zymkey Application Utilities library, libzk_app_utils. Systems intending to run such applications require that the `libzkapputils` package be installed.

This API facilitates writing user space applications which use Zymkey to perform cryptographic operations, such as:

1. Signing of payloads using ECDSA
1. Verification of payloads that were signed using Zymkey
1. Exporting the public key that matches Zymkey's private key
1. "Locking" and "unlocking" data objects
1. Generating random data Additionally, there are functions for changing the i2c address (i2c units only), setting tap sensitivity and controlling the LED.

Developers wishing to build applications which utilize the libzk_app_utils library should additionally install the `libzk_app_utils-dev` package, which contains the necessary development files for the Zymkey's C library. To install this package on a system that does not need to run the applications (e.g. a Docker container or when cross compiling on a foreign architecture), use `apt install --no-install-recommends libzkapputils-dev`. This will prevent `apt` from installing the Zymkey's `zkifc` driver daemon.

Usage:

```
#include <zymkey/zk_app_utils.h>
```

To add libzk_app_utils as a dependency of a CMake-based project, add the following lines to your project's CMakeLists.txt file:

```
find_package(zkAppUtils REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(target_name PRIVATE zkAppUtils::zk_app_utils)
```

Makefile-based projects may likewise configure the library dependency via pkg-config:

```
CFLAGS="$(pkg-config --cflags zkapputils)"
LDFLAGS="$(pkg-config --libs zkapputils)"
```

items.name: zkLockDataF2F
items.signature: int zkLockDataF2F(zkCTX ctx, const char *src_pt_filename, const char *dst_ct_filename, bool use_shared_key)
items.brief: Lock up source (plaintext) data from a file and store the results (ciphertext) in a destination file.
items.details: This function encrypts and signs a block of plaintext data from a file and stores the result in a destination file.

params.name: ctx
params.description: (input) Zymkey context.

params.name: src_pt_filename
params.description: (input) The absolute path to the file where the source (plaintext) data is located.

params.name: dst_ct_filename
params.description: (input) The absolute path to the file where the destination (ciphertext) data should be deposited.

params.name: use_shared_key
params.description: (input) This parameter specifies which key will be used to used to lock the data up. A value of 'false' specifies that the Zymkey will use the one-way key whereas 'true' specifies that the shared key will be used. Specify 'true' for publishing data to another that has the shared key (e.g. Zymbit cloud) and 'False' when the data is meant to reside exclusively withing the host computer.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

notes.text:
The zymkey has two keys that can be used for locking/unlocking operations, designated as 'shared' and 'one-way'.

1. The one-way key is meant to lock up data only on the local host computer. Data encrypted using this key cannot be exported and deciphered anywhere else.
1. The shared key is meant for publishing data to other sources that have the capability to generate the shared key, such as the Zymbit cloud server.

items.brief: Perform a raw ECDH operation.
items.details: Perform an ECDH operation with no Key Derivation Function (KDF). The raw pre-master secret is returned in the response. The peer public key is presented in the call.

params.name: ctx
params.description: (input) Zymkey context.

params.name: slot
params.description: (input) The key slot to use for the local key. If this parameter is -1, the ephemeral key is used.

params.name: peer_pubkey

params.name: peer_pubkey_sz
params.description: (input) Size of the peer public key.

params.name: pre_master_secret
params.description: (output) returned pointer to the pre-master secret

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for general failure.

items.brief: Perform a raw ECDH operation.
items.details: Perform an ECDH operation with no Key Derivation Function (KDF). The raw pre-master secret is returned in the response. The peer public key is referenced from the zymkey internal key store.

params.name: ctx
params.description: (input) Zymkey context.

params.name: slot
params.description: (input) The key slot to use for the local key. If this parameter is -1, the ephemeral key is used.

params.name: peer_pubkey_slot
params.description: (input) The peer public key slot where the peer public key is to be found.

params.name: peer_pubkey_slot_is_foreign
params.description: (input) If true, the peer public key slot is found in the foreign public keyring.

params.name: pre_master_secret
params.description: (output) returned pointer to the pre-master secret

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for general failure.

items.name: zkDoECDHAndKDF
items.signature: int zkDoECDHAndKDF(zkCTX ctx, ZK_ECDH_KDF_TYPE kdf_type, int slot, const uint8_t *peer_pubkey, int peer_pubkey_sz, const uint8_t *salt, int salt_sz, const uint8_t *info, int info_sz, int num_iterations, int derived_key_sz, uint8_t **derived_key)
items.brief: Perform an ECDH operation plus Key Derivation Function.
items.details: Perform an ECDH operation with Key Derivation Function (KDF). The derived key is returned in the response. The peer public key is presented in the call.

params.name: ctx
params.description: (input) Zymkey context.

params.name: slot
params.description: (input) The key slot to use for the local key. If this parameter is -1, the ephemeral key is used.

params.name: peer_pubkey
params.description: (input) The peer public key.

params.name: peer_pubkey_sz
params.description: (input) Size of the peer public key.

params.name: salt
params.description: (input) The salt to use for the selected KDF.

params.name: salt_sz
params.description: (input) The salt size. Must be less than or equal to 128 bytes.

params.name: info
params.description: (input) The info field to use for RFC 5869. Ignored for PBKDF2.

params.name: info_sz
params.description: (input) The size of the info parameter. Must be less than or equal to 128 bytes.

params.name: num_iterations
params.description: (input) Number of iterations to carry out (PBKDF only)

params.name: derived_key_sz
params.description: (input) The desired number of bytes to return for the KDF. For RFC 5869, this value must be less than 8160 bytes (SHA256) or 16320 (SHA512).

params.name: derived_key
params.description: (output) returned pointer to the derived key.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for general failure.

items.details: This function is called in order to wait for a perimeter breach event to occur. This function blocks the calling thread unless called with a timeout of zero. Note that, in order to receive perimeter events, the zymkey must have been configured to notify the host on either or both of the perimeter detect channels via a call to "zkSetPerimeterEventAction".

A 0 value means no breach has occurred on this channel. This array is allocated by this routine and so it must be freed by the caller.

items.name: zkSetBatteryVoltageAction
items.brief: Set battery voltage threshold action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the battery voltage falls below the threshold set by zkSetBatteryVoltageThreshold. If this function is never called, do nothing is default. There are three actions:

- Do nothing
- Go to sleep until battery is replaced
- Self-destruct

params.name: action
params.description:
(input) The action to apply, specify one of the ZK_THRESHOLD_ACTION_TYPE:

- Do nothing (ZK_ACTION_NONE)
- Sleep (ZK_ACTION_SLEEP)
- Self-destruct (ZK_ACTION_SELF_DESTRUCT)

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: zkSetBatteryVoltageThreshold
items.brief: Sets the battery voltage threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the battery voltage falls bellow, the action set by zkSetBatteryVoltageAction will be carried out. The recommended threshold is 2.3V. If this function isn't called 2.3V is assumed by default. Threshold must be below 2.5V.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in Volts.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: zkSetCPUTempAction
items.brief: Set HSM CPU temperature threshold action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the HSM CPU temperature falls below the threshold set by zkSetCPULowTempThreshold, or rises above the threshold set by zkSetCPUHighTempThreshold. There are two actions to apply:

- Do nothing
- Self-destruct

params.name: action
params.description:
(input) The action to apply, used it's named constant from ZK_THRESHOLD_ACTION_TYPE:

- Do nothing (ZK_ACTION_NONE)
- Self-destruct (ZK_ACTION_SELF_DESTRUCT)

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: zkSetCPULowTempThreshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU low temperature threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the on-board HSM CPU's tempreature falls below, the action set by zkSetCPUTempAction will be carried out. WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if you set a threshold above the CPU's ambient temperature. The recommended setting is no more than 20C. If no threshold is set, -10 degrees celsius is set as default.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in celsius.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: zkSetCPUHighTempThreshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU high temperature threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the on-board HSM CPU's tempreature rises above, the action set by zkSetCPUTempAction will be carried out. WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if you set a threshold below the CPU's ambient temperature. The recommended setting is no less than 40C. If no threshold is set, 65 degrees celsius is set as default.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in celsius.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: zkSetSupervisedBootPolicy
items.brief: Sets the Supervised boot policy.
items.details: This function specifies the action to take when Supervised boot event triggers based on a file change.

params.name: policy_id
params.description:
(input) The actions to apply to the Supervised boot process:

- 0 Do Nothing (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_NO_ACTION)
- 1 Self-Destruct (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_DESTROY)
- 2 Hold Chip in Reset (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_HOLD_RESET)

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.
